chapter: Discovering Henderson, clarinet and first gigs
title: Getting a clarinet, then a saxophone, and boyhood fellow players
summary: His father refused a clarinet but his mother arranged one; he played in the Commerce High School orchestra, borrowed a friend's saxophone and got his own alto for Christmas. He names schoolmates Freddy Jenkins, Benny Carter and Farley Jordan.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: But the first time you heard Buster

Oh, yes. Oh, yes, yes, yes. So I -- so then I went to my father. I said -- now, I've been taking violin lessons now about eight, nine, ten years. Steady, studying the violin, you know. I played in the high school orchestra up on 66th Street, used to be Commerce High School, and we won first prize in greater New York, the school orchestra, and I was one of the first violin players, you know. So my father, he couldn't hear of that, you know. He was of that old school, you know, he'd say, "What do you mean, buy you a clarinet?" And he told me no. "No," he said, "I'm not going to buy you no clarinet." But my dear mother was always in the background. She says -- so, lo and behold, I got a clarinet and started, you know, taking clarinet lessons, and again I'd say I liked it. I liked it too. I liked the clarinet. So about -- you know, so I started digging with those -- you know, we played simple marches, not the big time stuff like Washington Post" and all that. Not that hard stuff. We played, you know, sort of simple marches, kids, you know. So I got along on the clarinet pretty good. So then there was a -- so all the kids up and down the street, you know, some of them had saxophones, they had trumpets and trombones, and almost every kid you used to see on the street in those days had some kind of instrument in his hand. A violin or trumpet or, you know. So we all used to meet. Some kids had drums, you know, we'd meet and try to
play a little music, a little jazz or whatever. So I used to take this kid's saxophone, you know.

So about a couple years later, Christmas, and my mother told me, she says, "Go look in the closet over there. There's something in there for you." And I looked in there and there's a brand new saxophone and a case and --
Yeah. So I got the -- well, that's how I got started in the --
: Were there any other of those kids that stayed with the music that we might know of?
Yes. You know Freddy Jenkins who used to play with -- well, he was in this high school orchestra.

Yeah. Won the prize, and there's some who didn't. Benny Carter was along. Benny, he didn't go to the same school I did, and he didn't play in this orchestra, but he was along about that same time, and another fellow named Farley Jordan, he was a trombone player. He played a little bit professional. And there was a few of them who played, you know, professionally. Not -- they never got too big, but they played. They could play.
